results.rationale: CP17 requires a system of controls to manage hygiene. Section 4-3(3) mandates a system of controls at registered establishments to ensure compliance with conditions in sections 4-7A and 4-7B. Section 4-7A(2)(a) specifically requires the establishment to be kept in a clean and hygienic condition appropriate for the export operations and plant products. Parallel requirements for accredited properties exist in sections 3-1(3) and 3-3A(2)(a).

CP18 requires a system of controls to manage waste control and disposal. Section 4-3(3) requires a system of controls to ensure compliance with section 4-7A, which in subsection (2)(d) explicitly requires waste to be appropriately treated and disposed of. Parallel requirements for accredited properties are in sections 3-1(3) and 3-3A(2)(c).

CP19 requires the system of controls to be effective for the type of export operations and activities. Section 4-3(3) requires the system of controls to ensure that conditions in sections 4-7A and 4-7B 'will be complied with' in relation to those operations and products, which directly addresses effectiveness. Section 3-1(3) contains the identical requirement for accredited properties.

CP20 requires a system of controls to manage pests and contaminants including rodent control. Section 4-3(3) mandates a system of controls for compliance with sections 4-7A and 4-7B. Section 4-7A(2)(b) specifically requires pests and contaminants to be controlled in a manner appropriate for the export operations and plant products. Parallel provisions for accredited properties are in sections 3-1(3) and 3-3A(2)(b).

CP21 is identical to CP19, requiring the system of controls to be effective for the type of export operations. The same sections apply: 4-3(3) for registered establishments and 3-1(3) for accredited properties both require the system of controls to ensure compliance with prescribed conditions for the relevant operations and products.

CP22 requires at least 2 years of records demonstrating compliance with hygiene, waste, and pest control systems. Section 11-7(2) requires occupiers of registered establishments to retain relevant records for at least 2 years. Section 11-6(2) imposes the same requirement on managers of accredited properties. Section 11-2(1) sets general record requirements (English, dated, accurate, legible, auditable).

CP23 specifies record format requirements: in English, dated, accurate, legible, and auditable. Section 11-2(1) directly states these exact requirements: (a) in English; (c) dated; (d) accurate, legible and able to be audited. This is the sole governing provision for record format.

CP24 requires all establishment areas to be clean and hygienic appropriate for the export operations and plant products. Section 4-7A(2)(a) for registered establishments states this verbatim. Section 3-3A(2)(a) contains the identical requirement for accredited properties.

CP25 requires all areas to be maintained so prescribed goods are not or not likely to be infested by pests or contaminated. Section 4-7A(1)(b) for registered establishments states this exact requirement. Section 3-3A(1)(b) contains the identical requirement for accredited properties.

CP26 requires pest control stations/traps (e.g., rodent bait stations) to be fit for purpose and in good working order. No section explicitly mentions bait stations. The closest is section 4-7A(2)(b), which requires pests and contaminants to be controlled in an appropriate manner, implying control measures must be effective. Section 4-2(4)(c) requires design to minimise infestation possibility. This CP is not directly stated but inferred from these provisions.

CP27 appears to require chemical storage not to contaminate prescribed plants/products. Section 4-7A(2)(c) requires toxic substances (including fumigants, rodenticides, insecticides) to be managed and stored appropriately in accordance with State/Territory laws. Section 4-2(4)(c) requires design to minimise contamination. These are the governing provisions for chemical storage contamination prevention.

CP28 appears to require chemical storage not to contaminate areas where plants/products are prepared. The same provisions as CP27 apply: section 4-7A(2)(c) requires appropriate management and storage of toxic substances, and section 4-2(4)(c) requires design to minimise contamination. These govern contamination of preparation areas from chemical storage.
